description: Masala Chai is a quintessential Indian beverage, a soul-warming blend of robust black tea, aromatic spices, and creamy milk, sweetened to perfection. Each sip offers a comforting embrace of ginger, cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon, creating a truly invigorating experience. This traditional spiced milk tea is a daily ritual for many, perfect for any time of day.

ingredients.notes: strong, loose-leaf Indian tea like Assam or Darjeeling

instructions.title: Prepare the Spices
instructions.text: In a mortar and pestle, lightly crush the green cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon stick pieces, black peppercorns, and peeled ginger. You want to bruise them to release their aromatic oils, not grind them into a powder. Set aside the prepared spice mixture.

instructions.title: Boil Water and Add Spices
instructions.text: In a saucepan, combine the water and the crushed spice mixture. Bring the water to a rolling boil over medium-high heat. Let it boil for 2-3 minutes, allowing the spices to infuse deeply into the water and release their fragrant flavors.

instructions.title: Add Tea Leaves
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the loose black tea leaves to the boiling spiced water. Continue to simmer for another 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tea leaves have brewed and imparted their strong color and flavor to the liquid.

instructions.title: Pour in Milk and Sugar
instructions.text: Pour the milk into the saucepan with the tea and spices. Add the sugar to your desired sweetness. Stir well to combine all ingredients. Increase the heat slightly to bring the mixture back to a gentle boil.

instructions.title: Simmer for Flavor Development
instructions.text: Once the chai comes to a boil, reduce the heat to low and let it simmer gently for 5-7 minutes. This simmering step is crucial for the flavors to meld beautifully and for the chai to develop its rich, creamy texture and robust taste. Stir occasionally to prevent milk from sticking to the bottom.

instructions.title: Strain and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully remove the saucepan from the heat. Place a fine-mesh strainer over a serving pot or individual cups. Pour the Masala Chai through the strainer to remove all the tea leaves and whole spices. Discard the strained solids.

instructions.title: Enjoy Your Authentic Masala Chai
instructions.text: Serve the hot Masala Chai immediately. You can garnish with a pinch of ground cardamom or a tiny cinnamon stick, though it is traditionally served plain. Enjoy this comforting and invigorating Indian beverage.

tips: For the most authentic flavor, always use fresh, whole spices and crush them just before brewing. Pre-ground spices lose their potency quickly.
Adjust the amount of ginger, sugar, and tea to your personal preference. Some prefer a stronger ginger kick, while others like it sweeter or with more milk.
To achieve a frothy texture, after straining, pour the chai back and forth between two cups from a height several times before serving.
